alerts.title: EFV CNS toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list insomnia and abnormal dreams as persistent CNS toxicity of EFV, recommending dose reduction from 600mg to 400mg or substitution with DTG if symptoms persist. Patient has been on EFV since February 2024 and reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. These symptoms are classic EFV side effects with strong temporal drug attribution. No alternative causes are documented. The clinician's plan documents the complaints but proposes no management action.

evidence.recommended_action: Lower EFV dose to 400mg or substitute EFV with DTG if symptoms persist, per guideline toxicity management recommendations.

alerts.title: Viral load overdue per annual monitoring schedule
alerts.message: Guidelines require viral load monitoring every 12 months for adults with suppressed viremia. Patient's last viral load was 60 copies/mL on 2025-08-10, approximately 165 days before the current visit. ART was initiated in February 2024, so the next annual VL is due around August 2026. While not yet overdue at this visit, the clinician's plan includes no mention of scheduling the upcoming viral load test.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule the next routine viral load test due around August 2026 to maintain annual monitoring compliance.

Fewer adverse events lower the risk of treatment discontinuation. EFV 400 mg can be co-administered with Rifampicin-containing anti-TB treatment, with co-administration well tolerated and plasma concentrations maintained above the levels considered to be effective.
